model: manual (Claude Code session acting as reviewer)

findings.title: Projections are shown as bare numbers with no confidence framing
findings.description: Starting gravity, est. final gravity, and est. ABV are presented as authoritative figures. The research brief (see 'Recommended Calculator Outputs' / 'Confidence Labels') and goal.yaml v2's honesty constraint require labeling confidence: recipe-estimated vs measured vs biological. Without it the tool overstates precision and erodes trust.
findings.evidence: planner_form.png + batch_detail.png show 'STARTING GRAVITY 1.140 / EST. ABV 14.7%' with no 'estimated from recipe' qualifier and no source.
findings.suggested_change: Label the projection block as 'Recipe estimate' with a one-line note that measured readings are more accurate, per docs/research 'Confidence Labels'.

findings.title: No warning when potential ABV exceeds yeast alcohol tolerance
findings.description: The sample batch is OG ~1.140 (sack/high-gravity per docs/research 'Style and Gravity Ranges'); potential ABV to dry is ~18%, above every listed yeast tolerance. The brief ('Yeast-Limited Final Gravity Estimate', 'Yeast UX Recommendations') explicitly wants a warning: expect residual sweetness/stall risk, and high osmotic stress above 1.120. The tool silently shows a finished number instead.
findings.evidence: planner_form.png: OG 1.140 with a single est. FG and no risk flag for tolerance/osmotic stress.
findings.suggested_change: When potential-ABV-to-dry exceeds yeast tolerance, show 'potential ABV exceeds yeast tolerance — expect residual sweetness or a stall'; when OG > 1.120 show an osmotic-stress note. Cite the manufacturer-data caveat ('tolerance depends on conditions').

findings.title: Timeline implies calendar completion; no stable-gravity / backsweetening safety message
findings.description: The timeline shows phases ending on fixed dates ('Conditioning … Sep 10, 26'), which risks implying the batch is 'done' by the calendar. docs/research is emphatic: completion = stable gravity, not bubbling/calendar; and backsweetening/bottling sweet mead without stabilization is a real bottle-bomb safety issue. goal.yaml v2 lists both as safety constraints.
findings.evidence: batch_detail.png: timeline labeled Lag/Primary/Secondary/Conditioning with end date, no 'confirm with stable gravity' or backsweetening caution anywhere.
findings.suggested_change: Add a persistent note near the timeline: 'Estimated — confirm completion with a stable gravity reading, not the calendar or airlock.' Add a backsweetening/bottling safety caution where relevant.

findings.title: No way to enter a measured OG; recipe estimate is the only source of truth
findings.description: docs/research ('Prefer Measured OG') makes measured OG first-class: a measured hydrometer OG is far more accurate than a recipe estimate and should override it. The planner only estimates from honey; there is no measured-OG input, so the whole projection is assumption-heavy with no upgrade path to higher confidence.
findings.evidence: planner_form.png: inputs are honey type/amount, water, yeast, spices — no field for a measured original gravity.
findings.suggested_change: Add an optional 'Measured OG (hydrometer)' field. When present, use it as the gravity source of truth and switch the confidence label to 'Measured'.

findings.title: No nutrient (TOSNA/YAN) schedule — the highest-value missing domain tool
findings.description: Honey-must is nitrogen-poor; docs/research repeatedly identifies low YAN as the leading cause of stuck/sluggish mead and sulfur, and gives a concrete TOSNA Fermaid-O formula and schedule. A nutrient schedule is arguably the single most useful calculator a mead planner can offer, and maps directly to a v2 product_surface tool + calculator_completion metric.
findings.evidence: planner_form.png + batch_detail.png: nothing about nutrients, YAN, TOSNA, or staggered additions anywhere in the tool.
anti_goal_risk: Must label TOSNA as a community protocol, not scientific law (anti-goal).
findings.suggested_change: Add a TOSNA nutrient schedule (total Fermaid O + 24/48/72h + 1/3-break additions) from Brix/volume + yeast nitrogen need, with the community-protocol disclaimer. Likely exceeds the 200-line cap — propose as its own cycle.

findings.title: No crawlable knowledge base (yeast/honey/problem/style profiles)
findings.description: The site is a single client-only SPA with zero indexable content. The strategy doc's core lesson is that durable, database-backed entity pages (yeast strains, honey varietals, fermentation faults, styles) are what search engines discover and what builds trust. v2 puts these in scope. This is a multi-cycle build but the biggest discovery lever.
findings.evidence: Only routes are '/' and '/mead/[id]' (client state). No /yeast/*, /honey/*, /problems/* pages exist.
findings.suggested_change: Stand up structured data (yeasts.json etc., sourced) + database-backed entity pages with real URLs and internal links. Multi-cycle; start with yeast strain profiles drawn from docs/research.

findings.title: Timeline shows exact end dates instead of ranges
findings.description: docs/research ('Why Timeline Must Be a Range', 'Baseline Timeline Bands') is explicit that mead timelines must be ranges adjusted by OG strength, temperature, nutrient status, and gravity readings — never a single date. The current timeline renders precise phase end dates, overstating certainty.
findings.evidence: batch_detail.png: phases terminate on a fixed date ('Sep 10, 26') with no range or confidence.
findings.suggested_change: Express phases as ranges (e.g. 'primary 14-35 days for standard OG') and re-narrow from logged gravity, per the brief's bands + adjustment factors. Fold into a later timeline-accuracy pass.
